Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • setup.py appears to be a compatibility script that only calls setuptools.setup(); there is no evidence of extra command execution, downloads, or file manipulation during installation.
  • pyproject.toml uses the standard setuptools.build_meta backend, with no evidence of suspicious custom PEP 517 hooks.
  • No .pth, sitecustomize.py, or usercustomize.py files were identified in the provided extraction.
  • did_had/__init__.py imports/exports package symbols and defines metadata; no malicious import-time behavior is evident.
  • No console_scripts or other entry-point based automatic execution path was identified.

Theft/Exfiltration/Persistence/Lateral Movement/Obfuscation

  • Credential harvesting: no code was found that broadly searches environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI/package-registry tokens, or similar secrets.
  • Network/exfiltration: tests/test_did_had.py references raw.githubusercontent.com/chaisemartinPackages/did_had/main/tutorial_data.dta, but this appears to be a public test dataset download in a test/manual execution context, not evidence of theft or exfiltration.
  • Staging/archive: no evidence of harvested-file archiving, temporary staging, or base64 packaging was found.
  • Persistence: no evidence of cron, systemd, launch agents, shell profile modification, or background polling loops was found.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions, or CI token abuse was found.
  • Obfuscation/loaders: the eval match appears to be in a comment describing a Stata option (eval(grid_XX)), not Python dynamic execution. No malicious exec/eval/compile, base64/zlib/marshal loader, or staged payload evidence was found.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on SOURCES.txt, the included files look like a normal Python package layout (did_had, tests, README, LICENSE, pyproject/setup metadata).
  • No suspicious native binaries, hidden payloads, or unexpected executable files were evident in the provided content.
  • Dependencies (numpy, pandas, scipy, nprobust, plus optional dev/plot dependencies) are generally consistent with the package’s stated statistical/econometrics purpose. No evidence of malicious dependency insertion was identified.
  • Wheel/sdist mismatch could not be assessed from the provided sdist text extraction alone.

Additional Verification Needed
